t: Sikandar Lodi rebuilt Agra in 1504–1505 and made it his seat of government, and Babur took it after defeating Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526.
Akbar built the modern city on the right bank of the Yamuna and the Agra Fort, and his grandson Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal there from 1632.
Aurangzeb moved the court to Delhi in 1658, after which Agra passed to the Jats, the Marathas and the East India Company, and it became a district town of British India.
dyk: When Babur went to find a site for a garden at Agra, he wrote in his memoir that the country was so ugly and detestable that he crossed back over the river repulsed; he then planted gardens in every corner of the spot he had chosen.

f.founded: An ancient city on the left bank of the Yamuna is lost in the legends of Krishna and the Mahabharata; Sikandar Lodi rebuilt Agra in 1504–1505, and Akbar founded the modern city on the right bank in 1558.
f.where: On the banks of the Yamuna river in western Uttar Pradesh, India, about 230 kilometres south-east of Delhi, in the Braj region.
f.known: The Lodi seat of government; the capital of the Mughal Empire; the Agra Fort; the Taj Mahal; the tombs of Akbar and Itmad-ud-daulah; Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi; the rebellion of 1857
f.today: Agra is a city in Uttar Pradesh with a population of 1,585,704 at the 2011 census, and its Taj Mahal and Agra Fort are World Heritage Sites.
